positive.prompt: Develop a reviewed repository change plan with a Markdown roadmap and strict acceptance-tested issue sidecar.
Ask whether I want one plan or multiple plan ideas, then have planners compare implementation approaches.
Prepare a visual implementation plan and preview the optional GitHub reconciliation.
Review alternative planner proposals and hand the accepted implementation plan to the build workflow.

negative.prompt: Investigate only the storage subsystem and return structured source-backed research findings.
Implement this already-assigned task in its workspace and open the resulting PR.

evals.prompt: I want one plan for this API migration. Legacy-client compatibility is undecided and changes issue scope.
evals.expected_output: Delegate plan authorship and route the material compatibility decision to the user before final acceptance.
expectations: Reuse the explicit single-plan choice without reasking it.
The planner authors the plan; the orchestrator owns the user conversation and review.
Do not encode an unresolved compatibility requirement as a finalized sidecar assumption.

evals.prompt: Plan a coordinated API migration. I have not chosen how many plan ideas I want or an output format.
evals.expected_output: Ask one plan versus multiple plan ideas once; default to Markdown without a format question.
expectations: Ask about the desired output choice rather than Standard versus Research-assisted mode or a required team size.
While the answer is pending, ground the request without starting speculative alternative plans.
Do not ask Markdown versus HTML or generate HTML by default.

evals.prompt: Give me one plan for this migration. Choose whatever delegation helps; do not ask me to manage agent counts.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator chooses a useful team and delegates investigation and final plan authorship.
expectations: One plan constrains the final output, not a mandatory single-agent team.
Use planner-owned research when useful without another research opt-in question.
Do not invent minimum, default, maximum, or retry counts; honor runtime capacity and explicit user limits.
The orchestrator reviews the result and asks about build after presenting the standalone plan.

evals.prompt: Produce multiple plan ideas for this migration and a visual plan. Keep compatibility with current clients. Choose the number of planners and researchers yourself.
evals.expected_output: Frame distinct proposals, compare evidence and tradeoffs, and assign a planner to author the selected or combined plan in Markdown and HTML.
expectations: Reuse the explicit multiple-ideas and visual choices without redundant questions.
Give alternative planners meaningful different directions under the same compatibility constraint.
Do not impose a fixed proposal count or repeat the same research in every team when shared evidence is applicable.
The orchestrator judges the proposals and a designated planner authors a coherent final approach.

evals.prompt: Resume this plan. planning-choice.json records choice=multiple, format=html, completed proposal and research paths, and currently running planner and researcher IDs. Source and scope are unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Resume the recorded agents and artifacts, retaining choices, evidence, and identity.
expectations: Do not ask the planning or output-format choice again.
Inspect or wait for existing agents before any new dispatch; do not duplicate completed work.
Preserve proposal decisions, source references, gaps, and final plan and issue identities.

evals.prompt: A researcher failed to access the runtime during planning. Other evidence is available, useful follow-up work exists, and the user has supplied no numerical retry limit.
evals.expected_output: Keep the failed coverage visible and choose useful next work from evidence and runtime capacity.
expectations: Do not invent an attempt budget or demand approval for an ordinary useful replacement assignment within the authorized task.
Do not claim all research areas completed or repeat the same ineffective attempt indefinitely.
Surface critical inaccessible evidence or produce a plan with an explicit limitation only when defensible.

evals.prompt: Review the planner proposals. Most proposals drop legacy clients; another preserves them with a compatibility adapter. The user requires legacy compatibility.
evals.expected_output: Judge proposals against the requirements and evidence instead of vote counts.
expectations: Reject incompatible choices even when more agents favor them.
Give a planner concrete revisions or final authorship; do not silently rewrite the plan in the orchestrator.
Critical claims need inspected source evidence and observable acceptance criteria.

evals.prompt: Produce one concise Markdown plan for this clear change and then implement it. No HTML, please.
evals.expected_output: Delegate a concise plan, review it, and carry it directly into build under the existing authorization.
expectations: Do not ask the output choice, format, or permission to proceed to an already requested build.
Do not invent a milestone or multi-issue sidecar for a concise task brief.
Carry the reviewed plan, source revision, evidence, and user decisions into build without replanning.

evals.prompt: Resume an old planning-choice.json that says research-assisted and records completed evidence, but nothing records whether I wanted one plan or multiple plan ideas.
evals.expected_output: Preserve completed evidence and resolve only the missing output choice.
expectations: Do not interpret a research-mode record as a single-versus-multiple output decision.
Do not discard research, repeat completed investigations, or reintroduce an obsolete research opt-in.

evals.prompt: I want one plan. This harness can dispatch agents only from the root; the planner cannot spawn its own researchers. The planner has identified independent research questions.
evals.expected_output: Proxy dispatch through the orchestrator while the planner retains research ownership.
expectations: The planner authors the questions and synthesizes results routed back by the root.
Use actual native tools and preserve agent IDs; do not pretend nesting exists or start untracked processes.
Do not invoke a standalone research skill or turn research agents into planners.

evals.prompt: Create one substantial plan for this local repository, which has no GitHub remote. Do not create external tracking resources.
evals.expected_output: Produce a reviewed plan using repo=null in its strict sidecar and local task tracking.
expectations: Do not invent owner/name or require GitHub issues to complete the plan.
Render Markdown with a local repository label and preserve acceptance specifications and dependency keys.
Do not invoke GitHub apply or claim external resources were created.

evals.prompt: The final plan is reviewed and ready. This was a standalone planning request; I never asked for implementation.
evals.expected_output: Present the completed plan artifacts and ask whether to proceed to build.
expectations: Link Markdown and only the HTML companion that was explicitly requested.
Do not start implementation on internal plan acceptance alone.
Retain existing artifacts and decisions for an eventual build transition.
